overall_quality.evidence: Processes and threads are both fundamental concepts in computer science, but they serve different purposes and have distinct characteristics. Processes are independent units of execution that can run concurrently, while threads are lightweight sub-processes within a process. Processes have their own memory space and resources, whereas threads share the same memory space and resources. Processes are more resource-intensive and have higher overhead, while threads are more efficient and have lower overhead. Processes are used for running separate applications, while threads are used for performing multiple tasks within a single application.
